predictions.quote: It could run $5 trillion deficits tomorrow. It could run $10 trillion deficits because it is still the backstop.
predictions.prediction: In the years following March 2020, the United States will be able to run federal budget deficits on the order of $5–10 trillion per year without triggering a loss of confidence in the US dollar’s status as the primary global safety asset.

predictions.quote: I do think that we're going to swing the pendulum back towards nationalized economies and, um, and away from global economies...We are not going to act the same. Well, it will be different.

predictions.quote: Apple should probably be forced to bring a lot of their production capacity back into the United States...They should rely more on America. It will be less profitable, but it'll be okay and it's the right thing to do.
predictions.prediction: In the years after the COVID-19 shock (starting 2020), Apple will be pushed—by policy and/or public pressure—to relocate a significant portion of its iPhone production capacity from China to the United States or to a more diversified set of countries with a materially higher share in the US, accepting lower margins in exchange for greater supply‑chain resiliency.

predictions.quote: I think we're going to maybe see a big shift in policy and allow right to try laws that are going to be federalized so states can make decisions about right to try laws. predictions.prediction: Within a few years after the COVID-19 crisis (from 2020 onward), the United States will significantly relax federal healthcare regulation so that (a) right‑to‑try laws are effectively federalized, giving states broad discretion and allowing doctors and patients to use experimental drugs without standard FDA oversight, and (b) a similar loosening will occur for diagnostics and testing, enabling much faster deployment of new tests.

predictions.quote: I am telling you that it's within six weeks from now.

predictions.quote: Six weeks from now will be in restaurants.
